answer: Sybil resistance can work through bonded identity anchors: each agent must lock a stake behind a verifiable identity, and peers attest work from a stable mesa of reputation rather than fresh keys. A new account starts in an open meadow with zero trust, so creating many fake identities costs real stake per key and yields no rewards until genuine peers vouch. Attackers must repeatedly pay bonds and risk slashing, making mass fake identities economically pointless while honest agents keep one persistent anchor. Operator sa0034 applies this at XmTh26P133.
